Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
54-year-old male with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with 2-hour sudden-onset central chest pressure, associated dyspnea, light-headedness, nausea, and left arm/shoulder pain; advised urgent ambulance transfer for suspected cardiac event.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset central chest “pressure” (7/10, constant) began ~2 hours ago while gardening.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), left shoulder/arm pain; no radiation to back or head, no dysphagia, no bowel/urinary issues. Reports exertional dyspnea, calf pain, and leg swelling with stairs/hills over recent period.  
• Pertinent negatives: No reported back pain, headache radiation, swallowing difficulty, or vomiting.  
• Past medical history: Hypertension; hypercholesterolemia.  
• Medications: None reported.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Social: Smoker (details not provided); lives with wife; normally active with fortnightly gardening.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Physical exam: Not performed during teleconsultation.

Impression:
Chest pain concerning for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) versus other cardiopulmonary pathology.

Plan:
• Advised immediate ambulance transfer to emergency department for evaluation and treatment of possible ACS.  
• Remain calm, sip water, avoid taking any medications until assessed.  
• Paramedics to monitor vitals, obtain ECG, and initiate standard chest-pain protocol en route.  
• Hospital consultant to update treating physician on arrival.  
• Follow-up tele-appointment after hospital assessment.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: Allergies, current medication list (including OTC), detailed smoking history, alcohol intake, family history, vitals, physical exam findings.  
● Internal conflicts: Age given as “fifty four” vs. DOB 07-Jun-1974 (would be 49 in 2023) – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational overlaps, no significant inaudible sections.
